summary: A 1935 L-4 cab staffed into the early 1980s, scarred by a 1967 fire just short of its walls, now a Recreation.gov rental reached by a long trail.

access.note: Overnight rental via Recreation.gov; trail access only after a road washout cut off vehicle access. Listing as of 2026-10-04 showed the access road washed out by winter flooding, with repairs hoped for by the 2027 rental season.

events.note: Site prepared: telephone line run, trees topped for the view, cab lumber staged on the summit.
14x14-ft L-4 ground cab built by the U.S. Forest Service.
Ellis and Faye Ogilvie staffed the lookout together in the 1940s, after meeting by radio while posted at separate lookouts.
Used as a WWII Aircraft Warning Service site.
The Evergreen Fire, started by loggers on the mountain's south side, burned to within several hundred feet of the lookout.
Regular fire-season staffing ended in the early 1980s.

Listed on the National Register of Historic Places July 14, 1987, under a multiple-property listing for Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie fire lookouts (nominating party not stated on the NPGallery asset page). Conflicts with willhiteweb.com and Recreation.gov, which both attribute NRHP listing to the 1990s restoration.
Seattle Area Explorer Scout Search and Rescue Group adopted the lookout, with support from the Mountaineers and Quest School; the 141st Army Reserve Aviation Battalion airlifted materials.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, nominated by Ray Kresek.

corrections.current: Rental description (sourced from Recreation.gov/ridb) states the lookout was placed on the NRHP during 1990s volunteer restoration; willhiteweb.com independently repeats the same claim.
corrections.proposed: NPGallery's own NRHP asset record gives a listing date of July 14, 1987, a decade before the restoration effort described on Recreation.gov and willhiteweb.com. The two popular accounts agree with each other but disagree with the primary NRHP record; this should be reconciled or flagged in the record.
corrections.evidence: NPGallery AssetDetail page for NRIS 87001187 states a listing date of July 14, 1987 as part of a multiple-property submission; Recreation.gov's description ('During volunteer restoration efforts in the 1990s, the lookout was placed on the National Register of Historic Places') and willhiteweb.com ('During restoration it was placed on the National Register of Historic Places') both attribute the listing to the 1990s restoration instead.

corrections.proposed: No change recommended, but note that the Recreation.gov description (already embedded in this record's rental.description) gives 5,587 ft, about 100 ft higher than the NHLR figure used for elevation_m. Flagging for awareness only.
corrections.evidence: NHLR detail page lists elevation as 5,483 ft (1,671 m); Recreation.gov campground listing #234178 opens with 'elevation of 5,587 feet'.

sources.title: Evergreen Mountain Lookout, NRIS 87001187
sources.publisher: NPGallery Asset Detail, National Register of Historic Places, National Park Service

notes_for_editor: Good spread of sources for a rental-tier lookout: NHLR and firelookout.com agree on the 1935 build; NHLR and willhiteweb.com separately confirm WWII Aircraft Warning Service use (firelookout.com's cached page does NOT mention AWS use, despite an earlier draft citing it for that claim -- fixed during fact-check). willhiteweb.com (a hiking-guide site, used here beyond its usual access-only role because no better source turned up) supplied the Ogilvie staffing anecdote and the 1967 Evergreen Fire, which also matches the burn-scar language already in the record's own rental.description. The NRHP-date conflict is more interesting than first flagged: NPGallery's own asset page gives 1987, but BOTH Recreation.gov and willhiteweb.com independently say listing came out of the 1990s restoration -- two popular secondary accounts agreeing with each other against the primary NRHP record. Left as a flagged conflict rather than guessing; someone with the actual nomination PDF could settle it. Elevation also differs by about 100 ft between NHLR (5,483 ft) and Recreation.gov/willhiteweb/firelookout.com (5,587 ft, three sources agreeing), noted but not changed. Fact-check also caught that the story's claim about the 2026 closure reason was wrong: the live Recreation.gov listing attributes the current closure to a winter-flooding road washout (hoped fixed for the 2027 season), not a wildfire as an earlier draft stated -- corrected. Also removed an unsupported claim that the U.S. Forest Service nominated the property for the NRHP; NPGallery's page does not say who nominated it. No new photos found beyond what the record already has.
